title: Centre Asks Netflix to Keep Pakistani Series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' Out of India
excerpt: The Information and Broadcasting Ministry has told Netflix to adhere to its May 2025 advisory and honour its June 2025 commitment, after complaints over the Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan series due to premiere globally on December 4.
body:
• The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has asked Netflix to ensure that content originating in Pakistan is not streamed in India, and to stand by a commitment it gave the ministry in June last year, official sources said.
  • The direction follows complaints about the possible India release of "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo," whose trailer dropped on November 24; the first part is scheduled for global release on December 4.
  • The Urdu-language series is Netflix's first Pakistani original, stars Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan, and is based on Farhat Ishtiaq's novel of the same name.
  • Netflix has not publicly clarified whether the series will be available to Indian subscribers, and did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The Centre has asked Netflix to ensure that the Pakistani series "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" is not streamed in India, escalating a row that began with appeals from Indian film workers' bodies earlier this week. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has asked the platform to adhere to its advisory of May 8, 2025 and to honour the position it conveyed in June last year, when Netflix informed the ministry that it had made no film or series originating in Pakistan available to subscribers in India, official sources told news agencies.

The ministry acted after receiving several complaints and representations regarding the possible release in India of the series, Reuters reported. The trailer for the show was released on Tuesday, and the first part is scheduled to stream globally on December 4.

The series

"Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" is Netflix's first Urdu-language original series from Pakistan. Directed and produced by Momina Duraid, it is based on the Urdu novel of the same name by Farhat Ishtiaq and brings together Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Hania Aamir and Iqra Aziz, among others. The story follows six interconnected love stories across three generations, centred on relationships, family bonds and unresolved wounds.

The industry push

The government's intervention follows letters from the All Indian Cine Workers Association, which wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday asking that Pakistani series not be allowed to air in India, and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees, which also appealed for a prohibition on the programme's domestic release. The Videshi reported the film workers' body's request earlier this week. The ministry's direction to Netflix is the first government step in the sequence.

The 2025 advisory behind it

The May 8, 2025 advisory was issued in the wake of the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed, and during India's Operation Sindoor. Citing national security and cross-border linkages, it instructed OTT platforms and digital intermediaries to discontinue Pakistani films, web series, songs and podcasts with immediate effect, referring to provisions of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 concerning content that could affect India's sovereignty, security, diplomatic relations or public order, according to the Hindu BusinessLine.

What happens next

The immediate question is whether Netflix geo-blocks the series in India when the first part premieres on December 4. The platform has not publicly clarified its India plans for the show, and it did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. For viewers outside India, the global release proceeds as scheduled; for Indian subscribers, the ministry's position is that the 2025 advisory already settles the question.
